components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之) — marks movement and roads, as in 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; 逗 is stopping or luring, then to tease, as in 逗笑.
豆 (dòu) — same sound: 逗 dòu. 豆 also sounds out 痘 dòu and 头 tóu.

example.hanzi: 他讲的笑话把大家都逗笑了。
example.pinyin: Tā jiǎng de xiàohua bǎ dàjiā dōu dòu xiào le.
example.english: The joke he told made everyone laugh.
example.fact: 逗 also means 'a pause', which is why the comma is 逗号. As a verb it is common in 逗笑 'to make someone laugh' and 逗小孩 'to play with a child', and colloquially 你真逗 means 'you're hilarious'.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子很会逗人笑。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi hěn huì dòu rén xiào.
examples.english: This child is good at making people laugh.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝被爸爸逗得咯咯笑。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao bèi bàba dòu de gēgē xiào.
examples.english: The baby giggled as Dad played with her.

components.note: 王 (jade) — on the left, 王 is the jade radical, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 理 reason; jade is bright and shows itself.
见 (jiàn, see) is a close sound clue (xiàn) and also fits the meaning: appear so it can be seen.

example.hanzi: 他突然出现在门口。
example.pinyin: Tā tūrán chūxiàn zài ménkǒu.
example.english: He suddenly appeared at the door.
example.fact: 现 almost always appears in compounds: 现在 (now), 出现 (appear), 现金 (cash). Colloquially it can mean 'on the spot', as in 现做现吃 ('cook it and eat it fresh').

examples.hanzi: 我发现我的钱包不见了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ fāxiàn wǒ de qiánbāo bú jiàn le.
examples.english: I found that my wallet is missing.

examples.hanzi: 这个商店现在没有货。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shāngdiàn xiànzài méiyǒu huò.
examples.english: This shop has no stock at present.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — marks insects and bugs, as in 蚊, 蛇, 蝴; 蜘蛛 is a spider.
知 (zhī) gives the sound exactly: 蜘 zhī.
虫 (insect) — marks insects and bugs, as in 蚊, 蛇, 蝴; 蜘蛛 is a spider.
朱 (zhū) gives the sound exactly: 蛛 zhū, also in 珠 zhū and 株 zhū.

example.hanzi: 墙角有一只很大的蜘蛛。
example.pinyin: Qiángjiǎo yǒu yī zhī hěn dà de zhīzhū.
example.english: There is a very large spider in the corner of the wall.
example.fact: Spider silk is, by weight, stronger than steel and tougher than Kevlar, able to stretch to nearly 40% of its length before breaking without snapping. Scientists have long tried to mass-produce synthetic versions of it, since spiders themselves are too territorial and cannibalistic to farm efficiently. A single web strand thick enough to stop a passenger plane would theoretically require an enormous colony working in coordination — something researchers have only approximated with genetically engineered silkworms and bacteria.

examples.hanzi: 我在浴室里看到了一只蜘蛛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài yùshì lǐ kàn dào le yì zhī zhīzhū.
examples.english: I saw a spider in the bathroom.

examples.hanzi: 蜘蛛在窗边织了一张网。
examples.pinyin: Zhīzhū zài chuāng biān zhī le yì zhāng wǎng.
examples.english: A spider has spun a web by the window.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — marks animals, as in 猫 cat, 猪 pig, 猴 monkey; 狗 is a dog.
句 (jù) is a loose hint for gǒu; 够 gòu and 钩 gōu share it.
尸 (body, rump) — body-related words: 尿 urine, 屎 dung, 尾 tail, 屋 room; here the buttocks and what comes out.
比 (bǐ) is only a loose sound hint for pì.

example.hanzi: 别说这些狗屁话了,赶紧干活。
example.pinyin: Bié shuō zhèxiē gǒupì huà le, gǎnjǐn gànhuó.
example.english: Stop talking this nonsense and get to work.
example.fact: Dogs' noses contain up to 300 million olfactory receptors, compared to about six million in humans, letting them detect scents at concentrations of parts per trillion. This extraordinary sense of smell is why dogs are trained to sniff out everything from explosives and narcotics to early-stage cancers and diabetic blood-sugar crashes, often before any device can.

examples.hanzi: 你这是狗屁不通的借口。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè shì gǒupì bù tōng de jièkǒu.
examples.english: That's a nonsensical excuse.

examples.hanzi: 他说的都是狗屁，别信他。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de dōu shì gǒupì, bié xìn tā.
examples.english: What he says is all nonsense, so don't believe him.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks rivers and water, as in 河, 海, 江; 汉 is the Han River, which gave name to the Han dynasty and people.
土 (earth) — marks earth and ground, as in 地, 城, 墙; 堡 is an earthen fort.
保 (bǎo) gives the sound exactly: 堡 bǎo.

example.hanzi: 他午饭点了一个汉堡和薯条。
example.pinyin: Tā wǔfàn diǎnle yī ge hànbǎo hé shǔtiáo.
example.english: He ordered a hamburger and fries for lunch.
example.fact: Despite its name, the hamburger's exact origin is disputed, but its name traces back to Hamburg, Germany, where 19th-century immigrants brought a style of minced, salted beef called 'Hamburg steak' to the United States. The dish was later placed between two pieces of bread for portability, likely by German-American vendors at fairs and lunch counters around the turn of the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 我想吃一个汉堡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chī yí ge hànbǎo.
examples.english: I'd like to eat a hamburger.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的汉堡又大又好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de hànbǎo yòu dà yòu hǎochī.
examples.english: The hamburgers at this shop are big and tasty.

components.note: 心 (heart) — worry and suffering weigh on the heart; also in 想 think, 急 anxious.
串 (chuàn) rhymes with huàn but is only a loose sound clue.

example.hanzi: 他患了重感冒。
example.pinyin: Tā huàn le zhòng gǎnmào.
example.english: He came down with a bad cold.
example.fact: 患 is a formal verb for 'to suffer from' a disease, and it sits in 患者 'patient' and 患病 'to fall ill'. In everyday talk people say 得了 for catching a cold, so 患 sounds medical or written.

examples.hanzi: 他患有糖尿病。
examples.pinyin: Tā huàn yǒu tángniàobìng.
examples.english: He suffers from diabetes.

examples.hanzi: 医院里有很多患者。
examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn li yǒu hěn duō huànzhě.
examples.english: There are many patients in the hospital.

meanings: to feel a sense of urgency

components.note: 著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.
心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 急 is a heart in a hurry. The top is a variant of 及 (jí, reach), the same sound as in 级 and 极.

example.hanzi: 别着急,慢慢来。
example.pinyin: Bié zháojí, mànman lái.
example.english: Don't worry, take your time.
example.fact: When the brain perceives a threat, the amygdala triggers a rapid release of adrenaline and cortisol, redirecting blood flow toward muscles and away from digestion — the 'fight or flight' response first described by physiologist Walter Cannon in the early 20th century. Chronic anxiety keeps this system activated far longer than it evolved for, which is why prolonged stress is linked to problems like high blood pressure and weakened immunity.

examples.hanzi: 离考试还早，你不用着急。
examples.pinyin: Lí kǎoshì hái zǎo, nǐ búyòng zháojí.
examples.english: The exam is still a way off, so there's no need to worry.

examples.hanzi: 他等了很久，开始着急了。
examples.pinyin: Tā děng le hěn jiǔ, kāishǐ zháojí le.
examples.english: He had waited a long time and began to get anxious.

components.note: 冫 (water, ice) — 冲 is the simplified 沖: a water element (冫) beside 中, so water rushing; this form is a water cousin of 冰 and 冷.
中 (zhōng) — near sound — 冲 is chōng; 中 also sounds out 钟 zhōng.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 他一时冲动买了那辆车。
example.pinyin: Tā yīshí chōngdòng mǎile nà liàng chē.
example.english: He impulsively bought that car.
example.fact: In the late 1960s, Stanford psychologist Walter Mischel ran what became known as the 'marshmallow test,' offering young children one treat now or two if they could wait 15 minutes alone in a room with it. Decades of follow-up research linked the children's ability to resist immediate impulse with later outcomes like academic performance, though more recent studies suggest family stability and household resources play a larger role than the test alone implied.

examples.hanzi: 做决定时不要冲动。
examples.pinyin: Zuò juédìng shí búyào chōngdòng.
examples.english: Don't be impulsive when making decisions.

examples.hanzi: 我真想冲动一次，辞职去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhēn xiǎng chōngdòng yí cì, cízhí qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: I really want to act on impulse once and quit my job to travel.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 帽, 帮: a belt of cloth with pieces hanging from it.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 妈妈用带子把包裹绑好了。
example.pinyin: Māma yòng dàizi bǎ bāoguǒ bǎng hǎo le.
example.english: Mom used a strap to tie up the package.
example.fact: The three-point seatbelt, now standard in cars worldwide, was invented in 1959 by Swedish engineer Nils Bohlin at Volvo. Volvo made the patent freely available to every other car manufacturer, a decision credited with saving an estimated one million lives in the decades since.

examples.hanzi: 这个包的带子断了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bāo de dàizi duàn le.
examples.english: The strap of this bag broke.

examples.hanzi: 他系好鞋带子就出门了。
examples.pinyin: Tā jì hǎo xié dàizi jiù chūmén le.
examples.english: He tied his shoelaces and went out.

meanings: to perform on a musical instrument

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.
奏 (zòu) — to play music; as a part it sounds out 揍 zòu and 凑 còu.

example.hanzi: 她在音乐会上演奏了一首钢琴曲。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yīnyuèhuì shàng yǎnzòule yī shǒu gāngqín qǔ.
example.english: She performed a piano piece at the concert.
example.fact: The oldest known musical instruments are flutes carved from vulture bone and mammoth ivory, found in a cave in southwestern Germany and dated to roughly 40,000 years ago. Their finger holes were spaced carefully enough that researchers have been able to reconstruct and actually play reproductions, suggesting music-making is nearly as old as modern humans themselves.

examples.hanzi: 他会演奏三种乐器。
examples.pinyin: Tā huì yǎnzòu sān zhǒng yuèqì.
examples.english: He can play three instruments.

examples.hanzi: 乐队正在演奏一首老歌。
examples.pinyin: Yuèduì zhèngzài yǎnzòu yì shǒu lǎo gē.
examples.english: The band is playing an old song.

components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.
目 (eye) — sight, as in 看, 睛, 睡.
艮 (gèn) is a loose sound clue for yǎn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 很 hěn and 根 gēn.

example.hanzi: 我亲眼看到了那场车祸的发生。
example.pinyin: Wǒ qīnyǎn kàndàole nà chǎng chēhuò de fāshēng.
example.english: I saw that car accident happen with my own eyes.
example.fact: Psychologist Elizabeth Loftus's research beginning in the 1970s showed that eyewitness memory is far less reliable than most people assume — simply changing the wording of a question, like asking how fast a car was going when it 'smashed' versus 'hit' another car, measurably altered what witnesses later recalled. Her work has since been cited in thousands of legal cases and helped reveal that even confident, detailed eyewitness accounts can be partly or entirely false.

examples.hanzi: 我亲眼看见他把钱包放进了包里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qīnyǎn kànjiàn tā bǎ qiánbāo fàng jìn le bāo lǐ.
examples.english: I saw with my own eyes that he put the wallet in the bag.

examples.hanzi: 你应该亲眼去看看。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi qīnyǎn qù kànkan.
examples.english: You should go and see for yourself.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; 富 is a house full of goods, hence rich.
畐 (fú) gives the sound: 富 fù is close, as in 福 fú and 副 fù.
月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.

example.hanzi: 他年纪很小的时候家里就很富有。
example.pinyin: Tā niánjì hěn xiǎo de shíhòu jiālǐ jiù hěn fùyǒu.
example.english: His family was already wealthy when he was very young.
example.fact: Nearly all of the gold ever mined throughout human history — an estimated 190,000-plus metric tons — would fit into a cube roughly 22 meters on each side, small enough to sit within a typical soccer field. Because gold is virtually indestructible and rarely discarded, most of it mined over thousands of years, including from ancient Egyptian and Roman times, is still in circulation today, recycled into new jewelry, coins, or electronics.

examples.hanzi: 这位富有的商人捐了很多钱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi fùyǒu de shāngrén juān le hěn duō qián.
examples.english: This wealthy businessman donated a lot of money.

examples.hanzi: 这里的文化富有特色。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de wénhuà fùyǒu tèsè.
examples.english: The culture here is rich in character.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — 羊 is a symbol of good fortune, as in 美 and 祥; 善 is goodness and kindness, together with 口 (words).

example.hanzi: 她是一个心地善良的人。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè xīndì shànliáng de rén.
example.english: She is a kind-hearted person.
example.fact: 善 is the root of 善良 (kind), 友善 (friendly) and 善于 + verb, 'to be good at (doing)', which is a useful pattern for describing skills. 善 as a lone noun is tied to the moral idea of 'goodness', as in 善恶 'good and evil'.

examples.hanzi: 他很善良,总是帮助别人。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn shànliáng, zǒngshì bāngzhù biérén.
examples.english: He is kind and always helps others.

examples.hanzi: 她善于和人交流。
examples.pinyin: Tā shànyú hé rén jiāoliú.
examples.english: She is good at communicating with people.

components.note: 予 (give) — 幻 is 予 written reversed — giving turned around, an illusion.
见 (see) — seeing and perceiving, as in 现, 看, 视: 觉 is to sense and become aware (jué), also "sleep" (jiào) in 睡觉.
The top is a shape of 学 (xué), a loose sound hint from the traditional 覺.

example.hanzi: 长期缺乏睡眠可能会导致幻觉。
example.pinyin: Chángqí quēfá shuìmián kěnéng huì dǎozhì huànjué.
example.english: Long-term lack of sleep can lead to hallucinations.
example.fact: Charles Bonnet syndrome causes people with significant vision loss — from conditions like macular degeneration — to see vivid, detailed hallucinations of people, patterns, or animals that aren't there, even though they know rationally that the images are not real. Researchers believe the visual cortex, deprived of its usual steady stream of input, essentially starts generating its own imagery, a phenomenon first described by the Swiss naturalist Charles Bonnet in 1760 after observing it in his own grandfather.

examples.hanzi: 我昨晚好像出现了幻觉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn hǎoxiàng chūxiàn le huànjué.
examples.english: Last night I seemed to have an illusion.

examples.hanzi: 这只是你的幻觉，那里什么也没有。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì nǐ de huànjué, nàlǐ shénme yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: It's just your imagination; there's nothing there.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — a hand, as in 对, 寻, 守; with 圭 (a heap of earth) it means heaping earth to mark a border, then to seal.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 这本杂志的封面是一张著名摄影师拍的照片。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn zázhì de fēngmiàn shì yī zhāng zhùmíng shèyǐngshī pāi de zhàopiàn.
example.english: This magazine's cover is a photo taken by a famous photographer.
example.fact: The very first issue of Time magazine, published in March 1923, featured retired U.S. Speaker of the House Joseph G. Cannon on its cover — chosen not for major news but simply because he was about to retire and made for a recognizable face. Time's red-bordered cover design, adopted decades later, has since become one of the most enduring visual brands in publishing history.

examples.hanzi: 这本书的封面设计很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de fēngmiàn shèjì hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: This book's cover design is beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 她的照片登上了杂志封面。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhàopiàn dēng shàng le zázhì fēngmiàn.
examples.english: Her photo appeared on the magazine cover.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and trade, as in 财 wealth, 货 goods, 贵 expensive; 赚 is to earn.
兼 (jiān) is only a loose sound hint for zhuàn.
钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 铁, 银, 钟; early money was metal coins.
戋 (jiān) — near sound — 钱 is qián; 戋 also sounds out 浅 qiǎn and 线 xiàn, and means small or thin.

example.hanzi: 他靠做生意赚钱养家。
example.pinyin: Tā kào zuò shēngyì zhuànqián yǎngjiā.
example.english: He earns money running a business to support his family.
example.fact: The world's first paper currency was issued in China during the Tang and Song dynasties, around the 7th to 11th centuries, initially as promissory notes among merchants before the government took over printing it directly. Centuries later, when Marco Polo described paper money to Europeans in the 13th century, many considered the idea of trading mere paper for goods almost unbelievable.

examples.hanzi: 我想努力工作，多赚钱。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng nǔlì gōngzuò, duō zhuànqián.
examples.english: I want to work hard and earn more money.

examples.hanzi: 做这个生意赚钱吗？
examples.pinyin: Zuò zhège shēngyi zhuànqián ma?
examples.english: Does this business make money?

components.note: 纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — wrapping with thread; also in 红 red, 级 level.

example.hanzi: 小孩缠着妈妈要玩具。
example.pinyin: Xiǎohái chán zhe māma yào wánjù.
example.english: The child keeps pestering mom for a toy.
example.fact: 缠 shows up in both the literal (a vine 缠 around a tree) and the figurative: someone who 'clings and pesters' you is 缠着你, and a lingering illness or problem is 缠身. Compare 纠缠 'to entangle'.

examples.hanzi: 绳子缠在树枝上了。
examples.pinyin: Shéngzi chán zài shùzhī shang le.
examples.english: The rope got tangled around the branch.

examples.hanzi: 他被工作缠住了,没时间去。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi gōngzuò chán zhù le, méi shíjiān qù.
examples.english: He's tied up with work and has no time to go.

components.note: 羊 — a sheep's head with curved horns; the sheep radical, as in 美 beautiful, 群 flock. It also sounds out 样 yàng and 养 yǎng.

example.hanzi: 山上有很多羊。
example.pinyin: Shān shàng yǒu hěn duō yáng.
example.english: There are many sheep on the mountain.
example.fact: Chinese uses 羊 for both sheep and goats; to be precise you say 绵羊 (sheep) or 山羊 (goat). Its measure word is 只 or 头, and 羊 is the eighth animal of the Chinese zodiac.

examples.hanzi: 牧民在草原上放羊。
examples.pinyin: Mùmín zài cǎoyuán shang fàng yáng.
examples.english: The herdsmen are grazing sheep on the grassland.

examples.hanzi: 我今晚想吃羊肉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīnwǎn xiǎng chī yángròu.
examples.english: I want to eat lamb tonight.

components.note: 周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.
亠 (lid) — the top stroke group, as in 市 and 交. The sound-borrowed number; no meaning link. Memory aid: a lid on top of 八 (eight) ends up as six.
八 (eight) — the bottom part, as in 分 divide. Same shape as 'eight' but the number 六 does not come from it; use it as a visual memory aid.

example.hanzi: 我们周六去公园野餐吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōuliù qù gōngyuán yěcān ba.
example.english: Let's go have a picnic in the park on Saturday.
example.fact: Saturday is the only day of the week in English whose name comes directly from a Roman god — Saturn — rather than from a Germanic or Norse deity, unlike Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. The seven-day week itself likely originated with the ancient Babylonians, who associated each day with one of the seven visible celestial bodies known at the time, including the sun, moon, and five planets.

examples.hanzi: 周六我不上班。
examples.pinyin: Zhōuliù wǒ bú shàngbān.
examples.english: I don't work on Saturday.

examples.hanzi: 下周六是我的生日。
examples.pinyin: Xià zhōuliù shì wǒ de shēngrì.
examples.english: Next Saturday is my birthday.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做, 住; 偷 is a person stealing.
俞 (yú) is a loose hint for tōu; 愉 yú and 输 shū share it.
亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做, 住; 偷 is a person stealing.
俞 (yú) is a loose hint for tōu; 愉 yú and 输 shū share it.

example.hanzi: 他偷偷把礼物放进了她的包里。
example.pinyin: Tā tōutōu bǎ lǐwù fàng jìnle tā de bāo lǐ.
example.english: He secretly put the gift into her bag.
example.fact: The mimic octopus, discovered off the coast of Indonesia in 1998, can imitate the appearance and movement of at least fifteen other sea creatures, including venomous lionfish, sea snakes, and flatfish, to sneak past predators unnoticed. It changes not just color and skin texture but also body posture and swimming style depending on which animal it is impersonating.

examples.hanzi: 孩子偷偷吃了一块糖。
examples.pinyin: Háizi tōutōu chī le yí kuài táng.
examples.english: The child secretly ate a piece of candy.

examples.hanzi: 她偷偷地笑了。
examples.pinyin: Tā tōutōu de xiào le.
examples.english: She smiled secretly.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 按; 抗 is to resist or hold off.
亢 (kàng) gives the sound exactly: 抗 kàng, also in 炕 kàng.

example.hanzi: 两支球队在决赛中激烈对抗。
example.pinyin: Liǎng zhī qiúduì zài juésài zhōng jīliè duìkàng.
example.english: The two teams fiercely competed against each other in the final.
example.fact: The human immune system wages a constant, largely invisible war against pathogens, and one of its key weapons, the antibody, can take on roughly 10 billion different molecular shapes generated by randomly shuffling a limited set of genes. This combinatorial trick lets the body recognize and resist an almost limitless variety of viruses and bacteria it has never encountered before, without needing a separate gene for each one.

examples.hanzi: 我们要对抗疾病。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào duìkàng jíbìng.
examples.english: We must fight disease.

examples.hanzi: 他们不想和老板对抗。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen bù xiǎng hé lǎobǎn duìkàng.
examples.english: They don't want to confront the boss.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; city walls were made of earth.
成 (chéng) sounds exactly like 城; also in 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng.
土 (earth) — marks earth and ground, as in 地, 城, 墙; 堡 is an earthen fort.
保 (bǎo) gives the sound exactly: 堡 bǎo.

example.hanzi: 这座城堡建于中世纪,至今仍屹立不倒。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngbǎo jiànyú zhōngshìjì, zhìjīn réng yìlì bùdǎo.
example.english: This castle was built in the Middle Ages and still stands today.
example.fact: Neuschwanstein Castle in Bavaria, built in the late 19th century for King Ludwig II of Bavaria, was never intended as a serious military fortress — it was designed largely for aesthetics and privacy, complete with modern conveniences like running water and central heating unusual for its time. Its fairy-tale silhouette later directly inspired the design of Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle.

examples.hanzi: 我们参观了一座古老的城堡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen cānguān le yí zuò gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo.
examples.english: We visited an ancient castle.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们用沙子堆了一座城堡。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen yòng shāzi duī le yí zuò chéngbǎo.
examples.english: The children built a castle out of sand.

components.note: 虫 (insect, creature) — marks small creatures, as in 蛇 snake, 蚊 mosquito; in 蛮 it is part of an old, derogatory label for outsiders.

example.hanzi: 这家店的菜蛮好吃的。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de cài mán hǎochī de.
example.english: The food at this restaurant is quite tasty.
example.fact: As an adverb, 蛮 is a colloquial 'quite, rather', used as 蛮 + adjective + 的, especially in the south: 蛮好的, 蛮贵的. The original 'barbarian' sense survives in words like 野蛮 and is considered rude.

examples.hanzi: 这个电影蛮有意思的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège diànyǐng mán yǒu yìsi de.
examples.english: This movie is quite interesting.

examples.hanzi: 今天蛮冷的,多穿点衣服。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān mán lěng de, duō chuān diǎn yīfu.
examples.english: It's quite cold today; wear more clothes.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes, as in 阶 steps, 院, 陆; 降 is to go down a slope.
夅 (two feet going down) — shows descent, and gives the sound: 降 jiàng.
艹 (grass, plants) — plants and leaves: 花, 草, 叶; 落 is leaves falling.
洛 (luò) sounds exactly like 落; related to 各 gè in 路 lù.

example.hanzi: 飞机将在十分钟后降落。
example.pinyin: Fēijī jiāng zài shí fēnzhōng hòu jiàngluò.
example.english: The plane will land in ten minutes.
example.fact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 lasted only 12 seconds and covered about 120 feet, roughly the wingspan of a modern Boeing 747, before touching back down on the sand at Kitty Hawk. Orville Wright piloted that first flight, while Wilbur ran alongside, and the brothers took turns on four short flights that day, the longest lasting less than a minute.

examples.hanzi: 飞机已经安全降落了。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī yǐjīng ānquán jiàngluò le.
examples.english: The plane has already landed safely.

examples.hanzi: 气温明天会降落到零度以下。
examples.pinyin: Qìwēn míngtiān huì jiàngluò dào língdù yǐxià.
examples.english: The temperature will drop below zero tomorrow.

components.note: 工 (work, craft) — craft and skill — clever handiwork; also in 左, 差.
丂 (kǎo) — near sound — 巧 qiǎo; 丂 also sounds out 考 kǎo and 烤 kǎo.

example.hanzi: 真巧，我们又见面了。
example.pinyin: Zhēn qiǎo, wǒmen yòu jiànmiàn le.
example.english: What a coincidence, we meet again.
example.fact: 巧 covers both 'skill' (灵巧 nimble) and 'coincidence', as in 真巧! ('what a coincidence!') and 碰巧 ('happen to'). Look out: in 巧克力 (chocolate) it only supplies the sound qiǎo.

examples.hanzi: 这个小女孩手很巧。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo nǚhái shǒu hěn qiǎo.
examples.english: This little girl is very skillful with her hands.

examples.hanzi: 你来得正巧,我们刚要开饭。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lái de zhèng qiǎo, wǒmen gāng yào kāifàn.
examples.english: You came at just the right time; we're about to eat.

components.note: 乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.

example.hanzi: 警方最终抓到了那名杀人犯。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zuìzhōng zhuā dàole nà míng shārénfàn.
example.english: The police finally caught the murderer.
example.fact: Fingerprint identification became a standard forensic tool after Argentine police officer Juan Vucetich used it to solve a murder case in 1892, matching a bloody thumbprint at the crime scene to the suspect, a mother who had killed her two children. It was the first criminal case in the world solved using fingerprint evidence, years before fingerprinting became routine in police departments elsewhere.

examples.hanzi: 报纸上说杀人犯已经被抓住了。
examples.pinyin: Bàozhǐ shàng shuō shārénfàn yǐjīng bèi zhuā zhù le.
examples.english: The newspaper says the murderer has been caught.

examples.hanzi: 那个杀人犯被判了二十年。
examples.pinyin: Nàge shārénfàn bèi pàn le èrshí nián.
examples.english: That murderer was sentenced to twenty years.

components.note: 平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.
巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.hanzi: 他平常很少喝酒。
example.pinyin: Tā píngcháng hěn shǎo hējiǔ.
example.english: He rarely drinks alcohol under normal circumstances.
example.fact: The idea of the statistical 'average person' was popularized in the 1830s by Belgian astronomer and statistician Adolphe Quetelet, who applied methods used to track measurement errors in astronomy to human traits like height and weight. His concept of l'homme moyen, or 'the average man,' laid groundwork for modern statistics but has since been criticized because no single real person is actually average across every measurement at once.

examples.hanzi: 今天和平常一样，很安静。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān hé píngcháng yíyàng, hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: Today is the same as usual, very quiet.

examples.hanzi: 这只是一件很平常的小事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì yí jiàn hěn píngcháng de xiǎoshì.
examples.english: This is just an ordinary little matter.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 按 is to press with the hand, as in 按摩 massage.
安 (ān) — same sound, different tone — 按 is àn; 安 also sounds out 案 àn.
手 (hand) — marks hand actions, as in 拿, 打; 摩 is to rub with the hand.
麻 (má) gives the sound: 摩 mó is close, as in 魔 mó and 磨 mó.

example.hanzi: 做完按摩后我感觉身体轻松了很多。
example.pinyin: Zuò wán ànmó hòu wǒ gǎnjué shēntǐ qīngsōng le hěn duō.
example.english: After the massage, I felt much more relaxed.
example.fact: Massage is described in the Huangdi Neijing, or Yellow Emperor's Inner Canon, one of China's oldest medical texts compiled around 2,000 years ago, which recommended rubbing and pressing the body to treat various ailments. Similar practices appear independently in ancient Egyptian tomb paintings and Greek medical writings, suggesting massage arose as a healing method across multiple early civilizations without shared contact.

examples.hanzi: 我的肩膀很疼，想去按摩。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiānbǎng hěn téng, xiǎng qù ànmó.
examples.english: My shoulders ache and I want to get a massage.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸喜欢让我给他按摩。
examples.pinyin: Bàba xǐhuan ràng wǒ gěi tā ànmó.
examples.english: Dad likes me to give him a massage.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.
身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.

example.hanzi: 这个问题本身就很复杂。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí běnshēn jiù hěn fùzá.
example.english: This problem itself is very complicated.
example.fact: In 1931, mathematician Kurt Gödel proved his incompleteness theorems, showing that in any sufficiently powerful mathematical system, there will always be true statements that the system itself cannot prove using its own rules. Gödel's proof cleverly works by constructing a statement that essentially refers to itself, an idea similar to a sentence that says 'this sentence cannot be proven true.'

examples.hanzi: 他本身就是一名医生。
examples.pinyin: Tā běnshēn jiù shì yì míng yīshēng.
examples.english: He himself is a doctor.

examples.hanzi: 工作本身不难，难的是时间太紧。
examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò běnshēn bù nán, nán de shì shíjiān tài jǐn.
examples.english: The work itself isn't hard; the hard part is the tight schedule.

components.note: 疋 (foot) — the lower right. Dictionary story: an old man walking 疋 with a cane. Early forms show a person looking around, unsure. Treat as a memory aid.
矢 (arrow) — Dictionary reads it as a cane held by an old man; memory aid: an old man leaning on a stick, unsure which way — doubt, 怀疑.
犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.

example.hanzi: 警方正在审问一名主要疑犯。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài shěnwèn yī míng zhǔyào yífàn.
example.english: The police are interrogating a main suspect.
example.fact: The legal principle that a suspect is presumed innocent until proven guilty traces back at least to Roman law, but it was formally cemented in many modern legal systems through documents like England's Magna Carta of 1215 and later the French Declaration of the Rights of Man in 1789. Despite its long history, the presumption of innocence still varies significantly in how it is actually applied across different countries' courts today.

examples.hanzi: 疑犯昨晚已经被带走了。
examples.pinyin: Yífàn zuówǎn yǐjīng bèi dài zǒu le.
examples.english: The suspect was taken away last night.

examples.hanzi: 警察在找另一名疑犯。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài zhǎo lìng yì míng yífàn.
examples.english: The police are looking for another suspect.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摇 is to shake or rock.
䍃 (yáo) — same sound — 摇 is yáo; 䍃 also sounds out 谣 yáo and 遥 yáo.

example.hanzi: 他摇摇头，说不知道。
example.pinyin: Tā yáoyao tóu, shuō bù zhīdào.
example.english: He shook his head and said he didn't know.
example.fact: 摇头 (shake the head) signals 'no' and 点头 (nod) signals 'yes', just as in English. 摇 also names rock music as 摇滚, and 摇篮 means a cradle.

examples.hanzi: 小船在水里摇来摇去。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎochuán zài shuǐ li yáo lái yáo qù.
examples.english: The little boat rocks back and forth on the water.

examples.hanzi: 孩子向我摇手说再见。
examples.pinyin: Háizi xiàng wǒ yáo shǒu shuō zàijiàn.
examples.english: The child waved and said goodbye to me.

components.note: 女 (woman) — with a hand 又, a seized person: a slave. 奴 nú also sounds out 努 nǔ and 怒 nù.
彐 (hand/snout) — the top part, as in 当 and 归. Dictionary story: a hand (彐) threshing rice, as in 奴隶 slave; the shape is an old tangle of strokes, so memory aid only.
氺 (water-like strokes) — the bottom part, a variant of 水. Memory aid: a servant working near water, a slave to the grain.

example.hanzi: 历史书详细描述了古代的奴隶制度。
example.pinyin: Lìshǐ shū xiángxì miáoshùle gǔdài de núlì zhìdù.
example.english: The history book describes ancient slavery systems in detail.
example.fact: Historians estimate that the transatlantic slave trade forcibly transported over 12 million enslaved Africans to the Americas between the 16th and 19th centuries, with roughly 1.8 million dying during the ocean crossing itself. Britain formally abolished slavery throughout most of its empire in 1833, and the payments made to former slave owners as compensation were so large that the British government only finished paying off the associated debt in 2015.

examples.hanzi: 那个国家早就废除了奴隶制度。
examples.pinyin: Nàge guójiā zǎo jiù fèichú le núlì zhìdù.
examples.english: That country abolished the slave system long ago.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲了一个奴隶的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng le yí ge núlì de gùshi.
examples.english: This movie tells the story of a slave.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — marks movement on foot, as in 起 rise, 越 cross, 超 surpass; 赶 is chasing or hurrying to catch up.
干 (gān) — gives the sound — 赶 is gǎn, same syllable with a different tone; 秆 gǎn and 肝 gān share it.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 他跑得很快,很快就赶上了前面的人。
example.pinyin: Tā pǎo de hěn kuài, hěn kuài jiù gǎnshàngle qiánmiàn de rén.
example.english: He ran very fast and quickly caught up with the person ahead.
example.fact: The ancient Greek philosopher Zeno of Elea devised a famous paradox around the 5th century BC arguing that the swift Achilles could never actually catch up to a slower tortoise given a head start, because by the time he reached the tortoise's starting point, it would have moved slightly further, and so on infinitely. The paradox wasn't fully resolved until the development of calculus, which showed how infinitely many shrinking time intervals can still sum to a finite amount of time.

examples.hanzi: 你走慢点，等我赶上你。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zǒu màn diǎn, děng wǒ gǎnshàng nǐ.
examples.english: Slow down and wait for me to catch up with you.

examples.hanzi: 快点，我们要赶上最后一班车。
examples.pinyin: Kuài diǎn, wǒmen yào gǎn shàng zuìhòu yì bān chē.
examples.english: Hurry up, we need to catch the last bus.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 叫, 吗; 吓 is a shout that frightens.
下 (xià) — same sound — 吓 is xià, like 下.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 那部电影的结局真的很吓人。
example.pinyin: Nà bù diànyǐng de jiéjú zhēn de hěn xiàrén.
example.english: That movie's ending was really scary.
example.fact: The human startle reflex is one of the fastest reactions the body produces, triggering a blink and muscle tensing within about 100 to 150 milliseconds of a sudden loud noise — faster than a person can consciously register what caused it. Neuroscientists trace this reflex to a simple, ancient neural circuit in the brainstem, which explains why even people who know a scare is coming, like in a haunted house, still can't help but jump.

examples.hanzi: 半夜里突然有声音，真吓人。
examples.pinyin: Bànyè lǐ tūrán yǒu shēngyīn, zhēn xiàrén.
examples.english: A sudden noise in the middle of the night is really scary.

examples.hanzi: 别吓人了，我胆子很小。
examples.pinyin: Bié xiàrén le, wǒ dǎnzi hěn xiǎo.
examples.english: Stop scaring people; I'm quite timid.

components.note: 火 (fire) — marks fire and heat, as in 烧 burn, 灯 lamp, 烟 smoke; 熬 is simmering on a fire, then enduring hardship, as in 熬夜 stay up late.
敖 (áo) — same sound: 熬 áo. 敖 also sounds out 傲 ào and 遨 áo.

example.hanzi: 妈妈在厨房熬粥。
example.pinyin: Māma zài chúfáng áo zhōu.
example.english: Mom is cooking congee in the kitchen.
example.fact: 熬 has the sense 'to cook slowly' (熬汤, 熬粥) and 'to endure a hardship', and it is the second half of 熬夜, 'to stay up late'. The same character read āo is a less common dialect cooking word, so áo is the one to learn.

examples.hanzi: 他每天熬夜工作到很晚。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān áoyè gōngzuò dào hěn wǎn.
examples.english: He stays up late working every night.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶用小火熬了一锅汤。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai yòng xiǎohuǒ áo le yì guō tāng.
examples.english: Grandma simmered a pot of soup over low heat.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 枪 first meant a wooden spear; wood radical also in 棍 stick and 板 board.
仓 (cāng) hints at the sound — close to qiāng; the same part is in 抢 qiǎng and 苍 cāng.
凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查昨晚的枪击事件。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá zuówǎn de qiāngjī shìjiàn.
example.english: The police are investigating last night's shooting incident.
example.fact: Gunpowder was invented in China around the 9th century, originally by alchemists searching for an elixir of immortality rather than a weapon. It took several more centuries for the mixture of saltpeter, sulfur, and charcoal to evolve from fireworks and incendiary devices into the propellant used in early firearms, which then spread along trade routes to the Middle East and Europe by the 13th century.

examples.hanzi: 新闻里说市中心发生了枪击案。
examples.pinyin: Xīnwén lǐ shuō shì zhōngxīn fāshēng le qiāngjī àn.
examples.english: The news says a shooting happened downtown.

examples.hanzi: 他在枪击中受了伤。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài qiāngjī zhōng shòu le shāng.
examples.english: He was wounded in the shooting.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进; 迈 is a big stride.
万 (wàn) — near sound — 迈 is mài, from the traditional 邁 where 萬 gave the sound.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.
⺈ (bent figure) — the top part of 尔, a variant stroke group. 尔 is an old form of 'you'; today it appears mainly in foreign names like 比尔 Bill.
小 (small) — the bottom part and radical, as in 少 few. The shape does not explain 'you'; the character is now mostly sound-borrowed.

example.hanzi: 我的邻居迈克尔是一名医生。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de línjū Màikè'ěr shì yī míng yīshēng.
example.english: My neighbor Michael is a doctor.
example.fact: The name Michael comes from the Hebrew Mikha'el, meaning 'who is like God,' and it has remained one of the most enduring given names in Western history, borne by archangels, kings, and popes alike. It was the most popular boy's name in the United States for most of the 1970s through the 1990s, a run of popularity unmatched by almost any other name in that period.

examples.hanzi: 迈克尔是我大学的同学。
examples.pinyin: Màikè'ěr shì wǒ dàxué de tóngxué.
examples.english: Michael is my college classmate.

examples.hanzi: 迈克尔明天要来我家吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Màikè'ěr míngtiān yào lái wǒ jiā chīfàn.
examples.english: Michael is coming to my house for dinner tomorrow.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: achievement takes effort.
工 (gōng) gives the exact sound; 工 also means work.
大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.

example.hanzi: 他从小就在学习中国功夫。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù zài xuéxí Zhōngguó gōngfu.
example.english: He has been learning Chinese kung fu since childhood.
example.fact: The Shaolin Temple in Henan Province, China, founded around 495 AD, became closely associated with martial arts training partly out of necessity — monks in the remote mountain temple needed to defend themselves from bandits and, according to tradition, developed exercises to stay fit during long periods of meditation. Its style of combat training later influenced dozens of distinct martial arts across East Asia.

examples.hanzi: 他练了十年功夫，身体很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā liàn le shí nián gōngfu, shēntǐ hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He practiced kung fu for ten years and is in great shape.

examples.hanzi: 学外语需要花功夫。
examples.pinyin: Xué wàiyǔ xūyào huā gōngfu.
examples.english: Learning a foreign language takes time and effort.

components.note: 幺 (small/thread) — the dictionary radical, as in 么 and 幻. 乡 is simplified from 鄉 (village); the three strokes here look like a thread. Memory aid: a thread looping home to the village.
木 (tree) — marks trees and wood, as in 林, 树, 桥; a village among the trees.
寸 (cùn) hints at the sound: 村 cūn is close.

example.hanzi: 他退休后搬到乡村居住。
example.pinyin: Tā tuìxiū hòu bāndào xiāngcūn jūzhù.
example.english: After retiring, he moved to live in the countryside.
example.fact: In 2007, for the first time in recorded history, more than half of the world's population lived in cities rather than rural areas, a threshold the United Nations projects will rise to roughly two-thirds by 2050. The shift has been especially dramatic in China, where the urban population share roughly tripled between 1980 and 2020 as tens of millions of people moved from the countryside into rapidly growing cities.

examples.hanzi: 我爷爷住在乡村，空气很好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye zhù zài xiāngcūn, kōngqì hěn hǎo.
examples.english: My grandfather lives in the countryside, where the air is good.

examples.hanzi: 乡村的夜晚特别安静。
examples.pinyin: Xiāngcūn de yèwǎn tèbié ānjìng.
examples.english: Nights in the countryside are especially quiet.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室; 完 first meant complete, whole.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; 元 also sounds out 玩 wán, 院 yuàn and 远 yuǎn.
正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.

example.hanzi: 考古学家发现了一个几乎完整的古代花瓶。
example.pinyin: Kǎogǔ xuéjiā fāxiànle yī ge jīhū wánzhěng de gǔdài huāpíng.
example.english: Archaeologists discovered an almost completely intact ancient vase.
example.fact: Sue, discovered in South Dakota in 1990, is the most complete Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton ever found, with about 90% of its bones recovered — an extraordinary rarity in paleontology, where most dinosaur fossils survive as only scattered fragments. The skeleton sparked a legal battle over ownership that eventually resulted in a 1997 auction where the Field Museum in Chicago won it for $8.36 million, the highest price ever paid for a fossil at the time.

examples.hanzi: 请给我一份完整的名单。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí fèn wánzhěng de míngdān.
examples.english: Please give me a complete list.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事我只听了一半，不完整。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi wǒ zhǐ tīng le yíbàn, bù wánzhěng.
examples.english: I only heard half of this story, so it's incomplete.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and herbs, as in 花, 草, 茶; 苏 originally named the perilla plant, and is also short for Jiangsu and Soviet (苏联).
木 (wood, tree) — wood radical — 格 first meant a wooden frame or lattice, hence "pattern, standard"; compare 树 tree, 板 board.
各 (gè) — same syllable, different tone — 格 is gé; 各 also sounds out 阁 gé and 胳 gē.
兰 (orchid) — simplified from 蘭, which had the grass radical 艹 on top and 闌 giving the sound lán — a plant name.

example.hanzi: 他去苏格兰旅行时参观了很多古老的城堡。
example.pinyin: Tā qù Sūgélán lǚxíng shí cānguānle hěn duō gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo.
example.english: When he traveled to Scotland, he visited many ancient castles.
example.fact: Scotland is home to more than 600 million liters of whisky maturing in casks at any given time — more than a hundred liters for every person living in the country — because the spirit legally must age in oak barrels for at least three years before it can be called Scotch whisky. Some of that whisky is lost each year to evaporation through the porous wood, a phenomenon distillers poetically call 'the angels' share.'

examples.hanzi: 苏格兰的风景非常美。
examples.pinyin: Sūgélán de fēngjǐng fēicháng měi.
examples.english: The scenery in Scotland is very beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 他说话带着苏格兰口音。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà dài zhe Sūgélán kǒuyīn.
examples.english: He speaks with a Scottish accent.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 别太在意别人的看法。
example.pinyin: Bié tài zàiyì biérén de kànfǎ.
example.english: Don't care too much about what other people think.
example.fact: Psychologists have documented what's called the 'spotlight effect' — the tendency for people to dramatically overestimate how much others actually notice or care about their appearance and mistakes. In one well-known 2000 study, participants asked to wear an embarrassing T-shirt in front of strangers guessed that about 50% of onlookers would remember it, when in reality fewer than 25% did.

examples.hanzi: 你别在意，他没有恶意。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié zàiyì, tā méiyǒu èyì.
examples.english: Don't mind it; he meant no harm.

examples.hanzi: 我一点也不在意天气好不好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yìdiǎn yě bú zàiyì tiānqì hǎo bu hǎo.
examples.english: I don't care at all whether the weather is good.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫; 嘴 is a mouth or lips.
觜 (zuǐ) — same sound — 嘴 is zuǐ, like 觜.
巴 (bā) — 巴 gives the sound bā in 爸 bà, 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 疤 bā, so it is a useful sound clue.

example.hanzi: 他张开嘴巴打了个大大的哈欠。
example.pinyin: Tā zhāngkāi zuǐba dǎle ge dàdà de hāqian.
example.english: He opened his mouth and let out a big yawn.
example.fact: The human mouth hosts more than 700 different species of bacteria, making it one of the most microbially diverse habitats on the entire body, second only to the gut. Most of these microbes are harmless or even beneficial, helping to break down food and defend against harmful invaders, though an imbalance among them is linked to problems like cavities and gum disease.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝一直张着嘴巴笑。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao yìzhí zhāng zhe zuǐba xiào.
examples.english: The baby kept laughing with his mouth open.

examples.hanzi: 吃东西的时候请闭上嘴巴。
examples.pinyin: Chī dōngxi de shíhou qǐng bì shàng zuǐba.
examples.english: Please close your mouth when eating.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.hanzi: 在这个团队里,他一直是老大。
example.pinyin: Zài zhège tuánduì lǐ, tā yīzhí shì lǎodà.
example.english: In this team, he has always been the boss.
example.fact: For much of European history, the legal principle of primogeniture automatically passed a family's land, titles, and wealth to the eldest son, a system designed to keep estates intact rather than splitting them among multiple heirs. The practice shaped centuries of political and economic power in places like medieval England, and echoes of it persist today in some royal succession laws, though most have since shifted toward absolute primogeniture regardless of gender.

examples.hanzi: 我家老大今年上初中了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lǎodà jīnnián shàng chūzhōng le.
examples.english: Our eldest child is starting middle school this year.

examples.hanzi: 老大带着大家一起干活。
examples.pinyin: Lǎodà dài zhe dàjiā yìqǐ gànhuó.
examples.english: The boss leads everyone to work together.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 这条大道两旁种满了梧桐树。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo dàdào liǎngpáng zhòngmǎnle wútóngshù.
example.english: This avenue is lined on both sides with plane trees.
example.fact: Yonge Street in Toronto was once listed in the Guinness World Records as the world's longest street, stretching about 1,896 kilometers (1,178 miles) north from Lake Ontario, though later research revealed the measurement had mistakenly combined it with a separate highway. Its origins trace back to 1793, when it was built partly as a military supply road.

examples.hanzi: 这条大道通向市中心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo dàdào tōng xiàng shì zhōngxīn.
examples.english: This avenue leads to the city center.

examples.hanzi: 他们沿着大道一直往前走。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yán zhe dàdào yìzhí wǎng qián zǒu.
examples.english: They walked straight ahead along the avenue.

components.note: 手 (hand) — two hands joined in respect: bowing and saluting; compare 扌 in 拿 and 打.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talking and language, as in 说, 语, 请; 访 is to visit and ask.
方 (fāng) hints at the sound: 访 fǎng is close, as in 仿 fǎng and 纺 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 下周我要去拜访一位老朋友。
example.pinyin: Xià zhōu wǒ yào qù bàifǎng yī wèi lǎo péngyou.
example.english: Next week I'm going to visit an old friend.
example.fact: U.S. President Richard Nixon's 1972 visit to China ended over two decades of diplomatic isolation between the two countries and was watched by an estimated one billion people worldwide through television broadcasts. Nixon later called the trip 'the week that changed the world,' and it paved the way for the two nations to establish full diplomatic relations in 1979.

examples.hanzi: 周末我想去拜访老师。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xiǎng qù bàifǎng lǎoshī.
examples.english: This weekend I'd like to visit my teacher.

examples.hanzi: 他拜访了几位重要的客户。
examples.pinyin: Tā bàifǎng le jǐ wèi zhòngyào de kèhù.
examples.english: He paid visits to several important clients.

components.note: 詹 (zhān) — mostly a surname; as a part it sounds out 瞻 zhān and 蟾 chán.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women and female roles, as in 妈 mom, 姐 sister, 姑 aunt; 姆 is a nanny, as in 保姆.
母 (mǔ) — same sound — 姆 is mǔ, just like 母 (mother).
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 詹姆斯是这支球队最重要的球员。
example.pinyin: Zhānmǔsī shì zhè zhī qiúduì zuì zhòngyào de qiúyuán.
example.english: James is the most important player on this team.
example.fact: In 2023, LeBron James became the NBA's all-time leading scorer, surpassing Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's record that had stood for nearly 39 years. James reached the milestone while also holding records for career minutes played and games started, a combination that reflects both his scoring ability and his unusually long-lasting durability across two decades in the league.

examples.hanzi: 詹姆斯是我哥哥的名字。
examples.pinyin: Zhānmǔsī shì wǒ gēge de míngzi.
examples.english: James is my older brother's name.

examples.hanzi: 詹姆斯在办公室加班。
examples.pinyin: Zhānmǔsī zài bàngōngshì jiābān.
examples.english: James is working overtime at the office.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
互 (mutual) — the shape looks like two hooks locking into each other — a handy picture for "mutually" in 互相.

example.hanzi: 两国同意在经济上相互合作。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó tóngyì zài jīngjì shàng xiānghù hézuò.
example.english: The two countries agreed to cooperate with each other economically.
example.fact: Clownfish and sea anemones share one of nature's clearest examples of mutualism: the fish gain protection from predators by hiding among the anemone's stinging tentacles, to which they are immune thanks to a protective mucus coating, while the anemone benefits from the fish chasing off potential predators and parasites. Neither species is thought to be able to thrive as easily without the other in the wild.

examples.hanzi: 朋友之间要相互帮助。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou zhījiān yào xiānghù bāngzhù.
examples.english: Friends should help each other.

examples.hanzi: 我们相互认识很多年了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiānghù rènshi hěn duō nián le.
examples.english: We've known each other for many years.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.
木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.

example.hanzi: 科学家从月球上带回了岩石样本。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā cóng yuèqiú shàng dài huíle yánshí yàngběn.
example.english: Scientists brought back rock samples from the moon.
example.fact: The Apollo missions brought back a total of about 382 kilograms (842 pounds) of lunar rock, soil, and dust samples between 1969 and 1972, and much of it remains sealed in original, untouched containers at NASA today. Scientists deliberately preserved a portion unopened, anticipating that future analytical techniques not yet invented would be able to extract more information than was possible at the time of collection.

examples.hanzi: 医生需要一份血液样本。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng xūyào yí fèn xuèyè yàngběn.
examples.english: The doctor needs a blood sample.

examples.hanzi: 请先看一下样本，再决定要不要买。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiān kàn yíxià yàngběn, zài juédìng yào bu yào mǎi.
examples.english: Please look at the sample first, then decide whether to buy.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — here the ice form of 氵 (water): 决 first meant to break a dam, so a decisive break.
夬 (guài) is a loose sound clue for jué; 夬 also sounds out 快 kuài and 块 kuài.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.

example.hanzi: 他决不会向困难低头。
example.pinyin: Tā juébù huì xiàng kùnnán dītóu.
example.english: He will never bow to difficulties.
example.fact: The second law of thermodynamics states that the total entropy, or disorder, of an isolated system will never decrease over time — one of the few laws in physics considered essentially inviolable. Physicist Arthur Eddington once wrote that if a theory disagrees with this law, 'there is nothing for it but to collapse in deepest humiliation,' underscoring how central it is to modern physics.

examples.hanzi: 我决不会忘记你的帮助。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jué bú huì wàngjì nǐ de bāngzhù.
examples.english: I will never forget your help.

examples.hanzi: 这件事我决不同意。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ jué bù tóngyì.
examples.english: I absolutely won't agree to this.
